notes:
### 1. Apportionment Formula

* **Fact:** Georgia uses a **single sales factor** (a 100% gross receipts factor / one-factor formula) to apportion multistate business income. The gross receipts factor is the ratio of gross receipts from business done within Georgia to total gross receipts from business done everywhere.
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (effective since January 1, 2008; unchanged for 2025 and 2026).
* **Official Source:** 
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *2025 IT-611 Corporate Income Tax Booklet*: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/2025-it-611-corporate-income-tax-booklet
  * Georgia Code (O.C.G.A. § 48-7-31(d)(2)): https://www.legis.ga.gov/
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Apportionment and Allocation FAQ*: https://dor.georgia.gov/apportionment-and-allocation-faq

---

### 2. Sourcing of Receipts from Services and Intangibles

* **Fact:** Georgia employs **market-based sourcing**. Under Georgia law, when receipts are derived from business other than the sale of tangible personal property (including services), gross receipts are deemed derived from Georgia if received from customers within Georgia or if the receipts are otherwise attributable to Georgia's marketplace. Net investment income from intangible property held purely for investment purposes is allocated rather than apportioned (allocated to Georgia if the corporation's situs is in Georgia or if acquired as income from business done in Georgia).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Source:** 
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *2025 IT-611 Corporate Income Tax Booklet*: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/2025-it-611-corporate-income-tax-booklet
  * Georgia Code (O.C.G.A. § 48-7-31(d)(2)(A)(i)): https://www.legis.ga.gov/
  * Rules and Regulations of the State of Georgia (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 560-7-7-.03): https://dor.georgia.gov/rules-and-regulations

---

### 3. Industries with Their Own Apportionment Formula

* **Fact:** 
  * **Airlines / Air Transportation:** Corporations whose net business income is derived principally from transporting passengers or cargo in revenue flight apportion income using a specific three-factor formula:
    * Revenue air miles factor weighted at **25%**
    * Tons handled factor weighted at **25%**
    * Originating revenue factor weighted at **50%**
  * **Motor Carriers and Petroleum Pipeline Companies:** Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 560-7-7-.03 sets out specialized apportionment rules/ratios for freight and passenger motor carriers and pipeline transportation companies.
  * **Financial Institutions:** Apportion gross receipts under the Financial Institutions Business Occupation Tax (O.C.G.A. § 48-6-95; Form 900) based on gross receipts within Georgia over gross receipts everywhere, using specific industry receipt categories (interest on loans, fees, etc.).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Source:** 
  * Georgia Code (O.C.G.A. § 48-7-31(d)(2)(B)): https://www.legis.ga.gov/
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Form 900 Financial Institutions Business Occupation Tax Return*: https://dor.georgia.gov/
  * Rules and Regulations of the State of Georgia (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. r. 560-7-7-.03): https://dor.georgia.gov/rules-and-regulations

---

### 4. Form and Schedule Used to Compute Apportionment

* **Fact:**
  * **C-Corporations (Form 600):** Apportionment is computed on **Schedule 6** (*Apportionment of Income*) of Form 600. The resulting ratio from Schedule 6 (Column C) is entered on Page 2, Line 4 (Schedule 1) to determine the net business income apportioned to Georgia.
  * **S-Corporations (Form 600S):** Apportionment is computed on **Schedule 9**.
  * **Partnerships (Form 700):** Apportionment is computed on **Schedule 7** (*Apportionment of Income*).
* **Applicable Tax Years:** 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Source:** 
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Form 600 Corporation Tax Return*: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/form-600-corporation-tax-return
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *2025 IT-611 Corporate Income Tax Booklet*: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/2025-it-611-corporate-income-tax-booklet
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Form 700 Partnership Tax Return*: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/form-700-partnership-tax-return

### 1. Corporate Income and Franchise (Net Worth) Tax Nexus

* **Corporate Income Tax Nexus Standard:** Corporations that own property, do business in Georgia, or receive income from Georgia sources are subject to Georgia corporate income tax. 
  * "Doing business" is defined as being engaged within Georgia in any activities or transactions for the purpose of financial profit or gain, whether or not registered to do business in the state, whether or not maintaining an office or place of business within the state, and whether or not connected with interstate or foreign commerce (O.C.G.A. § 48-7-31(a)).
  * Having an employee in Georgia creates nexus (subject to P.L. 86-272 protections for sales of tangible personal property).
* **Franchise (Net Worth) Tax Nexus Standard:** Imposed on corporations for the privilege of doing business or exercising a corporate franchise in Georgia. Foreign corporations doing business, owning property in Georgia, or having taxable status under O.C.G.A. § 48-7-31 are subject to the tax (O.C.G.A. § 48-13-72). 
  * Under the Net Worth Tax Table, corporations with a net worth not exceeding $100,000 have a tax liability of $0, but a return must still be filed if the corporation has nexus.
* **Bright-Line / Factor-Presence Economic Nexus Threshold for Income/Franchise Tax:** **Not found.** Georgia statutes and Department of Revenue regulations do not provide a bright-line dollar or transaction factor-presence economic nexus threshold for corporate income or net worth tax.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax: https://dor.georgia.gov/corporate-income-and-net-worth-tax
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – C Corporations FAQ: https://dor.georgia.gov/c-corporations-faq
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – Net Worth Tax for Corporations FAQ: https://dor.georgia.gov/net-worth-tax-corporations-faq
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – 2025 IT-611 Corporate Income Tax Instructions Booklet: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/2025-it-611-corporate-income-tax-instructions-booklet/download

---

### 2. Remote Seller Economic Nexus Threshold (Sales and Use Tax)

* **Economic Nexus Thresholds:** A remote seller must register, collect, and remit Georgia sales and use tax if it meets either of the following criteria (O.C.G.A. § 48-8-2(8)(M.1); Policy Bulletin SUT-2019-02):
  * Gross revenue exceeding **$100,000.00** from retail sales of tangible personal property delivered electronically or physically into Georgia; **OR**
  * Conducted **200 or more** separate retail sales of tangible personal property delivered electronically or physically into Georgia.
* **Measurement Period:** The **previous or current calendar year**.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (in effect since January 1, 2020; unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – Policy Bulletin SUT-2019-02 (*Remote Sellers – Sales and Use Tax Obligations*): https://dor.georgia.gov/document/bulletin/sut-2019-02-sales-and-use-tax-obligations-remote-sellers/download
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – Out-of-State Sellers: https://dor.georgia.gov/out-state-sellers

---

### 3. Public Law 86-272 Protection

* **Stated Position:** 
  * P.L. 86-272 protects an out-of-state corporation from Georgia income tax if its Georgia activities are strictly limited to the solicitation of orders for sales of tangible personal property, provided the orders are sent outside Georgia for approval and are filled and shipped via common carrier from outside Georgia.
  * If business activities or employees go beyond mere solicitation, the statutory protection is lost.
* **Net Worth Tax Exception:** The Georgia DOR explicitly specifies that **P.L. 86-272 does not apply to the Georgia net worth (franchise) tax**. A corporation exempt from income tax under P.L. 86-272 is still required to file Form 600 or 600S and pay the net worth tax (if net worth exceeds $100,000).
* **Filing Requirements for Claiming P.L. 86-272:**
  * The corporation must check the **"PL 86-272"** box on the front page of Form 600 / Form 600S.
  * Enter **zero ($0)** on line 8, Schedule 1 of Form 600.
  * Complete the remaining schedules, attach a copy of federal Form 1120 or 1120S, and attach an explanatory statement indicating the basis for P.L. 86-272 protection.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – C Corporations FAQ: https://dor.georgia.gov/c-corporations-faq
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – 2025 IT-611 Corporate Income Tax Instructions Booklet (Page 10): https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/2025-it-611-corporate-income-tax-instructions-booklet/download
  * Georgia Department of Revenue – 2025 IT-611S S Corporation Income Tax Booklet: https://dor.georgia.gov/document/form/2025-it-611s-s-corporation-income-tax-instructions-booklet/download

notes:
### Individual Income Tax Rates
* **Tax Year 2025:** Flat rate of **5.19%**. Under House Bill 111 (amending O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20), Georgia transitioned to a flat individual income tax system, reduced to 5.19% for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2025.
* **Tax Year 2026:** Flat rate of **4.99%**. The rate is reduced from 5.19% to 4.99% effective for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Important Tax Updates*: https://dor.georgia.gov/important-tax-updates
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Film Tax Credit Resources (Withholding Rate Schedule)*: https://dor.georgia.gov/film-tax-credit-resources
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *2025 Summary of Enacted Legislation*: https://dor.georgia.gov/2025-summary-enacted-legislation

---

### Corporate Income Tax and Minimum Tax
* **Tax Year 2025:** Flat rate of **5.19%** of Georgia taxable net income. Under House Bill 1023 (amending O.C.G.A. § 48-7-21(a)), Georgia aligned the corporate income tax rate to match the individual income tax rate imposed under O.C.G.A. § 48-7-20.
* **Tax Year 2026:** Under O.C.G.A. § 48-7-21(a), the corporate income tax rate matches the individual rate, reducing to **4.99%** for taxable years beginning on or after January 1, 2026.
* **Minimum Tax:** **None** (no minimum corporate income tax is imposed under Georgia law).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax*: https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/business-taxes/corporate-income-and-net-worth-tax
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *IT-611 Corporation Income Tax Instruction Booklet*: https://dor.georgia.gov/it-611-corporation-income-tax-instruction-booklet
  * Georgia General Assembly, *HB 1023 (2024)*: https://www.legis.ga.gov/legislation/66750

---

### State Sales and Use Tax Rate & Local Jurisdictions
* **State Rate (2025 and 2026):** **4%** (unchanged between 2025 and 2026).
* **Local Jurisdictions (2025 and 2026):** **Yes**, local jurisdictions add local taxes (including LOST, SPLOST, ELOST, TSPLOST, MARTA, and MOST). Combined state and local sales tax rates across counties and special districts typically total between **6% and 9%** (for example, the City of Atlanta rate is 8.5%, and Clayton County–College Park is 9%).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Tax Rates*: https://dor.georgia.gov/tax-rates
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Sales Tax Rates – Current, Historical, and Upcoming*: https://dor.georgia.gov/sales-tax-rates-current-historical-and-upcoming
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Georgia Sales and Use Tax Rate Charts*: https://dor.georgia.gov/sales-tax-rates-current-historical-and-upcoming

---

### Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes
* **Corporate Net Worth Tax (Franchise Tax) (2025 and 2026):**
  * Georgia imposes an annual graduated **Net Worth Tax** on C corporations and S corporations for the privilege of doing business or exercising a corporate franchise in the state (O.C.G.A. § 48-13-72).
  * **Brackets / Rates:**
    * Net worth of **$100,000 or less:** **$0** (exempt from paying the tax under O.C.G.A. § 48-13-71, though an annual return must still be filed).
    * Over $100,000 up to $150,000: **$125.00**.
    * Over $150,000 up to $200,000: **$150.00**.
    * Brackets graduate up to a maximum tax of **$5,000** for net worth in excess of **$22,000,000**.
  * Foreign corporations apportion net worth based on an in-state ratio of property and gross receipts.
* **Statewide General Gross Receipts or Margin Tax:** **Not found** (Georgia does not impose a statewide general gross receipts or margin tax).
* **Local Financial Institutions Business License Tax (2025 and 2026):** Under O.C.G.A. § 48-6-95, counties and municipalities are authorized to levy a local business license tax on financial institutions of not more than **0.25%** of Georgia gross receipts, with a maximum local minimum tax of **$1,000.00**.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Corporate Income and Net Worth Tax*: https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes/business-taxes/corporate-income-and-net-worth-tax
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *Form PT-440 Return of Business License Tax Instructions*: https://dor.georgia.gov/pt-440-return-business-license-tax
  * Georgia Department of Revenue, *2025 IT-611 Corporate Income Tax Booklet*: https://dor.georgia.gov/it-611-corporation-income-tax-instruction-booklet

notes:
### 1. Individual Return Due Dates & Extension Rules

* **Due Date (Calendar-Year Filers):** April 15 of the following year (e.g., April 15, 2026 for tax year 2025; April 15, 2027 for tax year 2026). If the date falls on a weekend or state holiday, the deadline moves to the next business day.
* **Extension to File:**
  * Georgia grants an extension of up to **6 months** (to October 15).
  * An approved federal extension (**IRS Form 4868**) is automatically accepted without requiring a separate state form.
  * If a federal extension was not requested, taxpayers must submit **Form IT-303** (*Application for Extension of Time for Filing State Income Tax Returns*) on or before the statutory due date.
* **Payment Rules During Extension:**
  * An extension of time to file does **not** extend the time to pay.
  * Any tax due must be remitted by the original statutory due date using **Form IT-560** (*Individual and Fiduciary Income Tax Payment Voucher*) to avoid interest and late payment penalties (assessed at 0.5% per month up to 25%).
* **Applicability:** Tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia DOR Tax Due Dates: https://dor.georgia.gov/tax-due-dates
  * Georgia DOR Requesting an Extension: https://dor.georgia.gov/requesting-extension
  * Georgia DOR Form IT-303 Instructions: https://dor.georgia.gov/application-extension-time-filing-state-income-tax-returns

---

### 2. Corporate & Pass-Through Due Dates & Extension Rules

* **C Corporations (Form 600):**
  * **Statutory Due Date:** 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the tax year (April 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extension:** For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025, corporations receive **7 months** to file (to November 15 for calendar-year filers) if they obtain a federal extension (**IRS Form 7004**) or file Georgia **Form IT-303** (Georgia law provides one additional month beyond the 6-month federal extension).
  * Payment must be remitted by the statutory due date with **Form IT-560C**.
* **S Corporations (Form 600S):**
  * **Statutory Due Date:** 15th day of the 3rd month following the close of the tax year (March 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extension:** Granted up to **7 months** (to October 15 for calendar-year filers) with an approved federal extension or Georgia **Form IT-303**. Payment must be remitted by the statutory due date using **Form IT-560C**.
* **Partnerships / LLCs taxed as partnerships (Form 700):**
  * **Statutory Due Date:** 15th day of the 3rd month following the close of the tax year (March 15 for calendar-year filers).
  * **Extension:** Automatic **6-month extension** (to September 15 for calendar-year filers) with a federal extension (**Form 7004**) or state **Form IT-303**. Taxes must be prepaid by the statutory due date using **Form IT-560C**.
* **Applicability:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (7-month corporate extension effective for tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2025).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia DOR Corporate Income Tax Booklet: https://dor.georgia.gov/2025-it-611-corporate-income-tax-booklet
  * Georgia DOR S Corporation Income Tax Booklet: https://dor.georgia.gov/georgia-s-corporation-income-tax-booklet
  * Georgia DOR Partnership Income Tax Booklet: https://dor.georgia.gov/2025-it-711-partnership-income-tax-booklet

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity Tax (PTET)

* **Existence:** Yes (enacted under HB 149; O.C.G.A. §§ 48-7-21 and 48-7-23). S Corporations and Partnerships (including LLCs taxed as partnerships) may make an annual election to pay tax at the entity level.
* **Tax Rate:** By statute, the electing PTE rate matches the Georgia individual income tax rate for the corresponding tax year:
  * **Tax Year 2025:** **5.19%**.
  * **Tax Year 2026:** **4.99%** (rate reduced from 5.19% to 4.99% beginning January 1, 2026).
* **How to Elect:**
  * Check the designated election box on the return:
    * S Corporations: Check *"S Corporation elects to pay the tax at the entity level"* on **Form 600S**.
    * Partnerships: Check *"Partnership elects to pay the tax at the entity level"* on **Form 700**.
* **When to Elect:**
  * Must be made annually on or before the due date or extended due date of the entity's return.
  * The election is irrevocable after the applicable due date passes.
  * The election is binding on all owners, including nonresidents.
* **Applicability:** Tax years 2025 and 2026 (rate decreased from 5.19% to 4.99%).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia DOR HB 149 PTE Tax FAQ: https://dor.georgia.gov/hb-149-pass-through-entity-tax-faq
  * Georgia DOR Taxes for Partnerships: https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes-partnerships
  * Georgia DOR Important Tax Updates: https://dor.georgia.gov/important-tax-updates

---

### 4. Composite / Group Nonresident Returns for Pass-Through Entities

* **Existence:** Pass-through entities may file a composite return on behalf of eligible nonresident members in lieu of nonresident withholding (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 560-7-8-.34).
* **Return Form:** **Form IT-CR** (*Georgia Nonresident Composite Tax Return*).
* **Due Date & Extensions:** Due date and extension deadlines are the same as for individual returns (April 15 for calendar-year filers; extension requested via Form IT-303 or federal extension).
* **Interaction with Elective PTET:** If the entity elects to pay the PTE tax at the entity level, a composite return is **not** filed/required.
* **Applicability:** Tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia DOR Form IT-CR: https://dor.georgia.gov/it-cr-georgia-nonresident-composite-tax-return
  * Georgia DOR Regulation 560-7-8-.34: https://dor.georgia.gov/rules-department-revenue-chapter-560-7-income-tax-division-subject-560-7-4-net-taxable-income-individual

---

### 5. Estimated Taxes & Nonresident Withholding for Pass-Through Entities

* **Estimated Tax Requirements:**
  * **Electing PTET Entities:** Required to pay estimated taxes in the same manner as a C Corporation using **Form 602-ES** (or via the Georgia Tax Center) if net income for the tax year can reasonably be expected to exceed **$25,000**. Underpayment penalties are computed on **Form 600 UET**.
  * **Composite Filers:** Estimated tax payments for composite returns are made using **Form CR-ES** (*Composite Return Estimated Tax*) following individual installment due dates.
* **Nonresident Withholding (Non-Electing Entities):**
  * Under O.C.G.A. § 48-7-129 and Rule 560-7-8-.34, partnerships, S corporations, and LLCs must withhold on each nonresident member's share of Georgia-sourced taxable income.
  * **Rate:** **4%**.
  * **De Minimis Exception:** Withholding is not required if the nonresident member's annual share of Georgia taxable income is less than **$1,000**.
  * **Withholding Return & Payment:** Filed and paid using **Form G-7 NRW** (*Nonresident Withholding Return*).
  * **Withholding Due Date:** Due on or before the statutory due date for filing the entity's income tax return, **without regard to extensions** (e.g., March 15 for calendar-year entities). Failure to timely pay incurs a **25% penalty** plus interest.
  * **Exemptions from Withholding:** Members who file **Form NRW-Exemption** (partnerships/LLCs) or **Form 600S-CA** (S corporations) certifying agreement to pay Georgia tax directly; or if the entity pays elective PTET or includes the member on Form IT-CR.
* **Applicability:** Tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia DOR Form G-7 NRW: https://dor.georgia.gov/g-7nrw-nonresident-withholding-return
  * Georgia DOR Form CR-ES: https://dor.georgia.gov/cr-es-composite-return-estimated-tax
  * Georgia DOR Partnership Income Tax Booklet: https://dor.georgia.gov/2025-it-711-partnership-income-tax-booklet

---

### 6. Main Return Forms

* **Individual:**
  * **Form 500** (*Individual Income Tax Return*).
  * *(Note: Form 500-EZ was discontinued and is no longer accepted for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2025)*.
* **C Corporation:**
  * **Form 600** (*Corporation Income Tax and Net Worth Tax Return*).
* **S Corporation:**
  * **Form 600S** (*S Corporation Income and Net Worth Tax Return*).
* **Partnership / Multi-Member LLC:**
  * **Form 700** (*Partnership Tax Return*).
* **Composite Nonresident Return:**
  * **Form IT-CR** (*Nonresident Composite Tax Return*).
* **Nonresident Withholding Return:**
  * **Form G-7 NRW** (*Nonresident Withholding Return*).
* **Applicability:** Tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official Sources:**
  * Georgia DOR Individual Income Tax Forms: https://dor.georgia.gov/this-years-individual-income-tax-forms
  * Georgia DOR Partnership Tax Forms: https://dor.georgia.gov/taxes-partnerships
  * Georgia DOR Form IT-CR: https://dor.georgia.gov/it-cr-georgia-nonresident-composite-tax-return

proposals.value: Pass-through entities may file a composite return on Form IT-CR on behalf of eligible nonresident members, sharing the same April 15 statutory due date and extension rules as individual returns. A composite return is not filed or required if the entity elects into the pass-through entity tax.
proposals.snippet: In lieu of withholding, the entity may elect to file a composite income tax return for one or all of its nonresident members using Form IT-CR.

proposals.value: Electing pass-through entities must pay estimated taxes using Form 602-ES if net income is expected to exceed $25,000, while composite filers use Form CR-ES. Non-electing entities must withhold at a 4% rate on each nonresident member's Georgia taxable income exceeding $1,000, remitted on Form G-7 NRW by the entity's return due date without extensions.
